title: A House for the Room
premise: Ulyana Yarrow, a meticulous property surveyor, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House, a derelict estate whose rooms measure larger on the inside and whose mirrors lag a full second behind reality. Digging through deeds and diaries, he learns the house was built over a sealed well where, decades ago, the townsfolk drowned a wrongfully accused man — and the house has been appraising its visitors ever since, weighing their guilt. As the mirrors begin showing what the house intends rather than what is, Ulyana realizes he is trapped until sunrise, when the well 'refills' and takes a soul to balance its ledgers. To survive, he must expose the town's buried crime aloud within the house's hearing, choosing truth over the loyalty that protected the guilty — and at dawn the house releases him, its mirrors finally running a second ahead.
about_author: Hazel Brightwater is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent years cataloguing condemned properties across the English coast. Their fiction blends surveyor's precision with folk horror, exploring what old houses remember about the people who kept their secrets.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Ulyana Yarrow accepts an urgent appraisal of Hollowmere House, payable triple for a one-night assessment. His POV establishes his ritual precision — lights on, doors counted — and his quiet debt-ridden desperation. Emotional beat: uneasy ambition, the sense of a man who counts things because counting keeps the world honest.

chapters.title: Square Footage
chapters.summary: Ulyana surveys the house by daylight and finds the interior measurements refuse to reconcile: the east wing is nine feet wider inside than out. He notes it professionally, but the discrepancy itches. Emotional beat: professional confidence beginning to fray at the seams of a building that lies.

chapters.title: Inventory of Doors
chapters.summary: His ritual deepens — he counts seventeen doors, then eighteen on a second pass, though nothing opened. POV stays tight on Ulyana, with flashbacks to his father, a bailiff who taught him that every room keeps accounts. Emotional beat: dread disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Lag
chapters.summary: At dusk, Ulyana catches a mirror showing him turning his head one second after he actually does. He tests it with a dropped pen; the reflection drops it late. Emotional beat: vertigo — the first crack where the house stops pretending to be passive.

chapters.title: Deeds and Debt
chapters.summary: In the study, Ulyana finds the original deed naming a well on the parcel, later 'capped' — and a 1962 newspaper clipping about a drowned laborer, Tomas Bell, accused of a crime the town never proved. Emotional beat: the surveyor's instinct to appraise turns toward people.

chapters.title: Seventeen Doors, Eighteen Rooms
chapters.summary: Night falls fully. Ulyana maps the house and finds a room the mirrors show but the floor plans deny, behind where the well should be. The lag widens to two seconds. Emotional beat: the house is not haunted — it is auditing.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Want
chapters.summary: The reflections begin showing not Ulyana but other men — townsfolk of decades past — standing where he stands, mouths moving. He realizes the mirrors replay judgments. Emotional beat: horror curdling into recognition; he is watching a trial.

chapters.title: The Neighbor
chapters.summary: A knock: elderly Maren Cotter, whose family sold the house, warns him to leave before the well refills at sunrise. Her POV briefly takes over, revealing her father helped drown Tomas Bell and that the house 'took' her brother in 1974. Emotional beat: complicit grief.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana finds Maren's family diary: her father wrote that silence was loyalty, that exposing the town would 'break the village in half.' Ulyana recognizes his own habit of looking away from inconvenient measurements. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirrors now run five seconds behind, showing Ulyana things he hasn't done yet — walking toward the cellar. The house is forecasting him. Emotional beat: loss of agency; the appraised becomes the appraiser's subject.

chapters.title: The Well Room
chapters.summary: Ulyana forces the eighteenth door and finds the well chamber, dry and waiting, ringed with scratched tally marks — one per soul the house has taken. He understands sunrise means a refill. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of horror.

chapters.title: Voices in the Plumbing
chapters.summary: The pipes carry voices: the drowned man's last night, the mob's arguments, each neighbor's rationalization. Ulyana hears the town's sheriff — Maren's grandfather — declare Bell guilty to protect a friend. Emotional beat: fury at justice outside the law that failed.

chapters.title: Maren Returns
chapters.summary: Maren comes back with lantern and shotgun, intending to seal the house forever with Ulyana inside — her family's method of keeping the debt contained. Her POV: love for her dead brother warring with the lie that kept her family safe. Emotional beat: loyalty as a weapon.

chapters.title: Standoff in the East Wing
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Maren among the lagging mirrors, which show them both their worst memories a beat late. He refuses to leave and refuses to be the payment. Emotional beat: two keepers of secrets facing each other across the truth.

chapters.title: What the House Weighs
chapters.summary: The house tests Ulyana: mirrors show him his own small dishonesties — the appraisal he fudged, the complaint he ignored. He realizes the house doesn't punish guilt; it punishes concealment. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Confession Room
chapters.summary: Ulyana understands the house's terms: it was built as a courtroom over the well, and it refills only when truth stays buried. He begins speaking Tomas Bell's name and story aloud, room by room. Emotional beat: courage as testimony.

chapters.title: Maren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Cornered by the mirrors replaying her family's crime, Maren breaks and confesses her father's role, her brother's death, her decades of silence. The lag in the mirrors begins to shrink. Emotional beat: confession as exorcism.

chapters.title: The Refill
chapters.summary: Pre-dawn. The well chamber floods with black water rising through the floors, and the house begins closing doors, counting down. Ulyana and Maren race to the well room to finish the testimony before it seals. Emotional beat: desperate sprint against the house's own clock.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: At the well's edge, Ulyana declares the town's crime in full — names, dates, the sheriff's lie — while Maren corroborates. The water stops an inch from their feet, then drains, the tallies on the wall erasing one by one. Emotional beat: cathartic release; the ledger balances with truth, not blood.

chapters.title: Sunrise Appraisal
chapters.summary: Dawn. The house is only a house: measurements reconcile, doors number seventeen. Ulyana completes the appraisal honestly, marking the property condemned — not for ghosts, but for what it was built to hide. Emotional beat: quiet professional grace.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Ulyana files his report and, over the town's objections, delivers copies of the Bell evidence to the historical society, forcing the living town to reckon. Maren stands beside him at the archive. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, pursued anyway.

chapters.title: A Second Ahead
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ulyana passes the demolished house and finds one surviving mirror in the rubble — his reflection now moves a second ahead of him, showing him a man who no longer flinches. He leaves it facing the sky. Emotional beat: resolution; memory kept, loyalty to truth chosen at last.
